triage_candidates.statement: effective_axis_sigma (src/physics/layer2/estimate_store_fields.py) has a real caller trap: it prioritizes 'value' over 'reference_value' whenever value is not None, so a naive caller passing an unresolved-but-near-zero candidate value (value=delta) silently defeats the reserved-wide-sigma contract. G2 independently confirmed this is a genuine bug pattern (reproduced standalone: value=delta with delta=0 leaves sigma unwidened at 0.001; value=None correctly widens to 1.43). The implementer already fixed their own call site (value=None when status!=resolved) and flagged this in their result's Out-of-scope observations, but the seam's own docstring does not yet state this precedence rule as an explicit usage warning. Recommend a doc-note addition to effective_axis_sigma's docstring (or module docstring) making the value-beats-reference_value precedence and the value=None-when-unresolved pattern explicit, so a future caller (e.g. G3/G5 or another axis-status consumer) does not have to rediscover it from first principles or hit it as a live bug.
